## 假日固定收益市場簡報

美國固定收益市場因退伍軍人節休市，符合SIFMA建議的全日休市安排。假日期間，中國研議對政府債券利息課稅，巴西則提交收緊財政規則的法案，為主權債市帶來重要消息。企業融資方面，CoreWeave正籌備一筆至少$40億、可能取得投資級評等的貸款，延續其有擔保融資策略。

中國的徵詢直接涉及持有政府債券的收益。據知情人士透露，中國人民銀行向銀行調查，若對中央與地方政府債券利息課徵25%稅負，將如何影響需求。銀行在這兩個市場的持有比重各超過60%，其利息所得的稅務待遇，因而同時牽動投資需求與政府舉債成本。目前尚未確定是否實施，也未決定涵蓋既有持債或僅適用新發行債券。

巴西將財政撙節承諾推進至立法提案，包括在特定條件下降低實質支出成長上限，讓市場有更具體的依據評估財政整頓。不過，社會支出的保障措施，以及柴油補貼不計入財政目標的安排，仍限制了撙節範圍。企業端則持續透過客戶合約、設備與加盟收入籌資，CoreWeave規劃中的貸款與新證券化方案都是例子。美國債市恢復交易後，這些交易的條件與能否完成，將進一步檢驗借款人取得融資的能力。

## 全球利率、信用與主權動態

中國央行上月進行債券課稅調查，請參與銀行評估，在25%稅率下，需求將減少不到10%、20%、30%，或超過30%。據Bloomberg報導，這項調查並未確定是否開徵或實施時間；中國人民銀行與財政部未回應置評請求。目前，企業與個人持有這些證券的利息收入均免徵所得稅。

中央與地方政府債券合計規模約人民幣100兆元，潛在影響廣泛。華泰證券估計，若對所有流通政府債券利息課稅，機構投資人每年稅負將增加約人民幣4,590億元；若僅適用新發行債券，首年金額約為前者的十分之一。中央政府債券的稅制調整須修法，地方政府債券則可透過行政規則變更。

華泰的試算區分了維持稅後報酬所需的調整幅度與預期市場反應。若25%稅負全數反映於殖利率、使稅後報酬保持不變，10年期公債殖利率須提高52個基點；但華泰預期，新發行10年期債券實際升幅較小，約10至20個基點。國海證券也認為，地方政府債券的調整幅度，可能遠低於完整維持原稅後報酬所需的升幅。在稅收疲弱之際，取消免稅可增加稅收，但投資人要求較高殖利率，也可能推升政府融資成本。

中國另宣布，計劃在11月16日當週於香港發行至多$20億美元主權債。財政部擬議的發行延續跨幣別境外籌資安排，時間在預期於深圳舉行的美中元首會面之前。這為發債日程增添一筆美元交易，最終定價與需求仍待揭曉。

巴西政府週三提交法案，擬自2027年起，在財政目標有無法達成之虞時，將實質支出成長上限由2.5%降至2%。當初級收支落在目標容許區間的下緣範圍內，也可凍結支出，並削減租稅豁免、補貼及稅額抵減。規劃部長Bruno Moretti表示，整體調整應可使2027年初級財政收支改善500億至600億雷亞爾，往後年度的效果將更大。

投資人擔憂巴西債務占GDP比率超過80%、名目赤字超過GDP的9%，這項提案是政府進一步回應疑慮的措施。政府目標是明年達成相當於GDP 0.5%的初級盈餘，亦即不含利息的財政盈餘，並於2030年提高至1.5%。當局擬保障必要社會福利，同時檢討無效租稅優惠與異常偏高的公部門薪資。不過，法案也容許將至多105億雷亞爾的柴油補貼排除於2026年財政目標之外。

這樣的組合，可能仍無法滿足期待停止最低工資實質調升、並採取更深度撙節的投資人。Bradesco Asset Management的Ana Rodela與BB Asset的Guilherme Novaes均懷疑，政府能否提出足以在選前恢復信心的措施。方案仍須透過立法變更落實；魯拉未來的經濟團隊人選，以及明年底前應完成的四名央行理事任命，也將影響政策前景。

智利財政部長Jorge Quiroz首次承認經濟陷入衰退，同時將經濟成長約4%的預測達成時間，由2030年總統任期結束時提前至2028年。季度原始數據顯示，第1季與第2季分別萎縮0.25%及0.02%；央行四捨五入後公布的數字則為先下滑0.3%、其後持平。Quiroz將疲弱主要歸因於銅產量受到衝擊，並以非礦業活動轉強與投資計畫，作為預期復甦的依據。

他雖認為燃料價格上漲只是暫時現象、通膨預期仍穩定，也表示不反對央行以更強力措施因應通膨。談到國營銅業公司Codelco的長期融資，他認為未來可能需要在母公司層級引入民間資本，但須維持國家控制權，並經過廣泛政治討論；政府近期計畫並不包括這項變更。他也建議出售非核心資產。Quiroz預測，全國銅產量可在五年內由今年不到500萬公噸回升至550萬至600萬公噸，新計畫則還需兩至三年才會影響產量。

CoreWeave籌備中的借款，是企業融資最明確的新進展。知情人士向Bloomberg表示，摩根士丹利與三菱日聯金融集團正牽頭安排一筆至少$40億的潛在貸款，最快下週向投資人推介，並可能分階段聯貸。預期將以晶片及相關客戶合約作為擔保，計畫仍可能變動。

儘管CoreWeave本身為非投資級，公司預期這筆融資可取得投資級評等。管理層初步討論的可能殖利率為7%至7.5%。今年3月以Meta客戶合約擔保的$85億投資級融資，可作為結構上的比較：其中一部分浮動利率為SOFR加2.25個百分點，另一部分則以約5.9%的固定利率融資；浮動利差只是其利息成本的一部分。公司調高銷售展望後，這筆新貸款將拓展融資管道，但執行長Michael Intrator仍排除以目前利率進行無擔保借款。

Intrator表示，營業利益成長快於利息費用，並預測2028年淨利可轉正；他也提出增加客戶預付款，作為替代資金來源。D.A. Davidson的Gil Luria仍質疑公司降低債務的能力，理由是利息費用高於調整後營業利益。Bloomberg的Odd Lots另指出，約13萬枚GPU的合約將於2027年到期，管理層認為這可在不增加資本支出的情況下帶來額外收入。由Steph Choe領軍的花旗分析師則認為，潛在施工延誤可能提高既有設施與開發中計畫的價值，並區分已存在的產能與尚待完工的項目。

CoreWeave客戶的需求也有新消息。據知情人士透露，OpenAI第3季營收達$100億，較前季增加近50%，接近去年同期的三倍。Anthropic首次公開發行的認購訂單達可供配售股數的數倍，《金融時報》報導，銀行家正考慮將估值提高至$1.5兆或以上，高於初步條件。不過，投資人Jack Selby仍持懷疑態度，警告若上市首日表現不佳，可能引發更廣泛的AI修正。Theory Ventures的Tomasz Tunguz表示，過去兩週AI融資洽談採用的營收倍數更保守；B Capital的Howard Morgan也表示，正建議新創公司尋求較低估值。已報導的營收增長、這筆發行的強勁需求，與民間資金在洽談時更審慎挑選投資標的的情況並存。

據知情人士透露，Newton Commercial Finance正與投資人初步討論一筆可能達$1.8億的設備貸款與租賃證券化，其中AI晶片貸款約占擔保資產15%。這家由Apple Bank與Eagle Point Credit Management合資的公司，預期Morningstar DBRS給予的評等將介於AAA至BB級。此前，Stonebriar上月發行$8.69億、GPU曝險約15%的證券化商品；Wingspire於9月完成的交易超過$4.07億，GPU曝險約20%。Newton的條件尚未定案。

Crunch Fitness正探索由Guggenheim Securities安排、以加盟收入支持的約$8億融資。擬議結構包括向機構投資人銷售、平均年限五年的$6.5億債券，$1億私募延遲撥款票據，以及$5,000萬可變動融資額度。初步討論的五年期利差為基準利率加230至250個基點；相較之下，Planet Fitness去年證券化交易中約五年期債券的利差為160個基點。Crunch最快下週啟動發行，條件仍可能變動。Neighborly本週另完成$2.75億發行，為全企業證券化市場增添交易。

新發行之外，個別借款人的協商仍在進行。據知情人士透露，JetBlue的多數債權人群體簽署合作協議，禁止與加入該協議的貸款人另訂私下交易。IHeartMedia正探索出售部分或全部Podcast業務以籌措現金。黑石則正推介一檔預計至少募集$30億的基金，擬以低於淨資產價值的價格，買進其他管理人旗下核心型不動產基金權益，回應該領域持續存在的流動性需求。

企業債需求的新分析顯示，家庭追求利息收入是重要支撐。由Dominique Toublan領軍的巴克萊策略師上月撰文指出，截至9月，個人投資人已向追蹤綜合指數的高評級債券基金投入$2,680億，幾乎為2025年同期的兩倍；這些基金約四分之一持倉為企業債。散戶目前持有高評級與高收益企業債市場約17%，為2022年初以來最高。Janus Henderson的Bradford Smith將部分需求歸因於退休族尋求長期收入；道明證券的Hans Mikkelsen則提醒，即使殖利率具吸引力，價格進一步下跌仍可能削弱買進意願。

貨幣政策方面，費城聯準銀行總裁Anna Paulson提出支持逐步緊縮的不同論點。這位有投票權的決策官員週二晚間表示，薪資壓力仍有限，通膨預期也與2%目標一致。若預期上升、薪資加速成長，或基礎通膨走高，她會支持加快行動，但目前未見這些情況。她形容基礎通膨停留在2.5%至3%之間，認為漸進步調可讓家庭、企業與金融機構有時間調整。芝加哥聯準銀行總裁Austan Goolsbee在週二另一場訪談中表示，服務業通膨持續尤其令人憂慮，並拒絕限制下次會議可採取的選項。緊縮速度與何種情況下應加快步調，仍是官員意見分歧之處。

英國則出現更強硬的獨立評估。英國國家經濟及社會研究院（NIESR）週三發布研究指出，即使英國央行再升息一次，通膨直到2030年底仍將高於2%；該院主張明年將利率升至5%，以提前約18個月控制通膨。其擔憂集中在通膨超過4%時進行的薪資談判，以及每季調整的能源價格上限，後者可能使家庭天然氣與電費在1月提高約四分之一。住宅建商Taylor Wimpey同時預測，全年營業利益將落在£2.62億至£2.99億區間的下緣，排除合資事業的完工交屋數為10,500戶。截至11月8日，訂單由去年同期的7,253戶降至6,839戶，反映較高房貸利率與生活成本限制買方需求。澳洲第3季住宅貸款創紀錄下滑15.5%，也呈現另一市場在高利率下借款需求減弱的情況。

美國房貸申請則略有改善。截至11月6日當週，美國房貸銀行協會（MBA）的30年期合約利率下降9個基點至7.21%，連續第四週下滑。購屋貸款申請增加7.5%，為4月中以來最大升幅，但僅是8月底以來第二次單週增加。再融資申請增加4.5%，連續第三週成長，水準仍接近2025年1月以來低點。整體申請量在前週下降1.2%後回升6.2%；市場指數由192.6升至204.6，購屋指數由131.4升至141.2，再融資指數由517.5升至540.7。這些週資料反映假日前的住宅融資狀況。

南韓對十多家銀行與券商開出創紀錄的1.63兆韓元、約合$12億的聯合壟斷罰款。南韓公平交易委員會表示，初級交易商於2020年1月至2023年6月間，在150場政府債券標售中交換投標殖利率資訊，或協調殖利率及投標量，其中145場查獲具體協議。KB證券遭罰3,322億韓元，金額最高。遭刑事告發的七家公司為KB、NH Investment & Securities、Mirae Asset、韓國中小企業銀行、Kiwoom、韓國產業銀行及Korea Investment & Securities。委員會認為，這些行為破壞標售競爭並造成政府損失，形成針對主權債分銷體系的重大執法行動。

兩項央行領導人事問題也有進展。Bloomberg報導，聯準會內部正討論紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams是否須在2027年6月滿65歲時退休，或可留任至2028年6月、在該職位任滿十年；關鍵在於如何計算他先前擔任舊金山聯準銀行總裁的年資。Williams預期任職至2028年，目前尚未宣布正式遴選程序，也不清楚主席Kevin Warsh或聯準會理事會是否支持提早離任。加拿大方面，經濟學家列出Jean Boivin、Jean-François Perrault、Nicolas Vincent、Carolyn Wilkins、Paul Beaudry與Carolyn Rogers，作為Tiff Macklem的可能接班人；Macklem任期於6月屆滿。加拿大央行總裁由該行董事會任命，須經政府批准，上述人選目前仍屬初期可能名單。

德國獨立經濟顧問將2026年成長預測由5月的0.5%上修至1.3%，2027年預測由0.8%調至1%，理由是政府支出與出口韌性，同時警告赤字擴大。能源供給方面，沙烏地阿拉伯向OPEC通報，10月產量增加26%至每日1,056萬桶；伊拉克通報每日產量接近490萬桶，高於協議上限。伊朗一名高層官員拒絕交出濃縮鈾，使和平進程的一項核心障礙仍未解決。另據牛津經濟研究院的聖嬰現象脆弱度研究，厄瓜多、秘魯與印尼的曝險排名最高，其農業、礦業與發電結構，是天候衝擊影響經濟活動與成本的傳導管道。

## 下一交易日觀察

美國市場恢復交易時，將迎來11月12日的勞動與住宅數據。截至11月7日當週初領失業救濟金人數預估為19.5萬人，前值18.9萬人；截至10月31日當週續領人數預估171萬人，前值171.8萬人，兩者均於UTC 13:30公布。10月成屋銷售於UTC 15:00公布，共識預估385萬戶，前值399萬戶。成屋銷售數據將顯示，近期房貸申請改善之際，實際完成的住宅銷售是否也已轉強。

週四聯準會官員談話包括Beth Hammack於UTC 14:00、Michael Barr於15:00、Goolsbee於16:30、Mary Daly於18:10，以及Williams於23:30發言。Paulson對漸進緊縮提出的條件，以及Goolsbee對服務價格的憂慮，使市場更關注12月9日決策前，是否有更多官員支持加快步調。

假日休市後，美國財政部預定於UTC 18:00標售30年期公債，4週、8週與17週國庫券則安排在16:30。長債標售將提供觀察市場對長天期利率曝險需求的新依據。UTC 19:00公布的10月聯邦預算收支，預估赤字為$2,986億；聯準會資產負債表與準備金餘額數據隨後於21:30公布。

UTC 17:00公布的能源庫存，將在波斯灣產量回升、外交問題未解之際，提供實體供給面的進一步資訊。共識預估截至11月6日當週，原油庫存減少110萬桶、汽油減少10萬桶、餾分油減少100萬桶。即使生產國恢復供給，庫存結構仍有助判斷燃料成本壓力能持續多久。

融資日程也延伸至恢復交易之後。CoreWeave潛在貸款將檢驗以晶片及客戶合約擔保可取得的借款條件；Newton設備資產擔保證券（ABS）與Crunch加盟收入證券化，則涉及不同擔保資產與投資人群體。Anthropic預定11月18日定價、11月19日開始交易，將使強勁訂單面對民間投資人對估值的疑慮。中國擬議美元主權債發行安排在11月16日當週。中國債券利息課稅的立法進展與適用範圍，以及巴西國會對財政方案的處理，仍各自影響政府融資成本。

overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國固定收益市場因退伍軍人節休市。中國央行向銀行調查，研議對中央與地方政府債券利息課徵25%稅負；兩個市場合計約人民幣100兆元，銀行在各市場的持有比重均超過60%。目前尚未確定是否開徵，以及涵蓋既有持債或僅適用新發行債券。華泰預期，新發行10年期債券殖利率將上升10至20個基點，低於其試算中完整維持原稅後報酬所需的52個基點。

恢復交易時，11月12日勞動與住宅數據、聯準會對緊縮速度的談話，以及30年期美國公債標售，將為政策預期與長天期債券需求提供新依據。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Holiday Fixed-Income Brief

U.S. fixed-income markets were closed for Veterans Day, in line with SIFMA's full-close recommendation. China's exploration of a tax on government-bond interest and Brazil's submission of tighter fiscal rules supplied consequential sovereign news during the holiday, while CoreWeave prepared a potential investment-grade loan of at least $4 billion that would extend its use of secured financing.

The Chinese consultation reaches directly into the economics of holding sovereign debt. The People's Bank of China asked lenders how a 25% tax on interest from central and local government bonds would affect demand, according to people familiar with the survey. Banks hold more than 60% of each market, making the treatment of their interest income important to both investor demand and public borrowing costs. Whether authorities proceed, and whether existing holdings or only new issuance would be affected, remain unresolved.

Brazil moved from promises of fiscal restraint to proposed legislation, including a conditional reduction in the ceiling on real spending growth. The package offers a more concrete basis for assessing consolidation, although its protections for social spending and an exclusion for diesel subsidies leave important limits. Across corporate financing, CoreWeave's planned loan and new securitization proposals showed borrowers continuing to seek capital through customer contracts, equipment and franchise revenue. Their terms and completion will provide fresh tests of funding access when U.S. bond trading resumes.

## Global Rates, Credit, And Sovereign Developments

China's central bank conducted its bond-tax survey last month, asking participating lenders to indicate whether demand would fall by less than 10%, 20%, 30% or more than 30% under a 25% levy. Bloomberg's account said the survey did not establish whether a tax would be introduced or its timing. The PBOC and Ministry of Finance did not respond to requests for comment. Interest on the securities is currently exempt from income tax for enterprises and individuals.

The potential scope is substantial: central and local government bonds together total roughly 100 trillion yuan. Huatai Securities estimated that taxing interest on all outstanding government bonds would add about 459 billion yuan to institutional investors' annual taxes. Applying a levy only to new issuance would make the first-year amount roughly one-tenth as large. Tax changes for central government bonds would require a legal amendment; changes for local government debt could be made through administrative rules.

Huatai's calculations illustrate the difference between a full tax adjustment and its expected market response. Preserving the same after-tax return under a fully reflected 25% levy would imply a 52-basis-point increase in 10-year government yields, the brokerage estimated. It expects the actual increase on newly issued 10-year bonds to be smaller, around 10-20 basis points. Guohai Securities similarly judged that the adjustment on local government bonds would probably be considerably smaller than the increase required to preserve the entire after-tax return. Ending the exemption could strengthen tax collection amid weak revenue, while higher required yields could raise the government's financing costs.

China also announced plans to sell up to $2 billion of dollar sovereign bonds in Hong Kong during the week of November 16. The Ministry of Finance's proposed offering extends offshore fundraising across currencies and comes ahead of an expected meeting between the U.S. and Chinese presidents in Shenzhen. It adds a new dollar transaction to the issuance calendar without establishing its eventual pricing or demand.

Brazil's government submitted legislation Wednesday that would cap real spending growth at 2% from 2027, down from 2.5%, when compliance with the fiscal target is at risk. It would also permit spending freezes when the primary balance is within the target's lower tolerance band and reduce tax exemptions, subsidies and credits. Planning Minister Bruno Moretti said the overall adjustment should improve the primary fiscal result by 50 billion-60 billion reais in 2027, with a larger effect in later years.

The proposed rules advance the government's response to investor concern about a debt ratio above 80% of GDP and nominal deficits exceeding 9% of GDP. The administration targets a primary surplus, excluding interest, of 0.5% of GDP next year and 1.5% in 2030. It intends to protect essential social benefits and review ineffective tax breaks and unusually high public-sector salaries. At the same time, the bill would allow up to 10.5 billion reais of diesel subsidies to be excluded from the 2026 fiscal target.

That combination is likely to fall short of investors seeking an end to real minimum-wage increases and deeper restraint. Bradesco Asset Management's Ana Rodela and BB Asset's Guilherme Novaes expressed skepticism about the prospect of measures strong enough to restore pre-election confidence. The package still needs legislative changes, while Lula's future economic-team choices and four central-bank board appointments due by the end of next year remain consequential for the policy outlook.

Chile's finance minister, Jorge Quiroz, acknowledged recession for the first time while bringing forward his forecast for growth of about 4% to 2028 from the end of the presidential term in 2030. The underlying quarterly figures show contractions of 0.25% in Q1 and 0.02% in Q2; rounded central-bank figures show a 0.3% decline followed by no change. Quiroz attributed the weakness chiefly to copper-production shocks and pointed to stronger non-mining activity and investment projects as reasons to expect recovery.

He also said he would see no problem with a stronger central-bank response to inflation, even while describing the fuel-price increase as temporary and expectations as anchored. His longer-term financing comments concerned state-owned Codelco: he said private capital at the parent-company level might eventually be needed, with state control preserved and broad political discussion required. Such a change is outside the government's immediate plans. He also suggested selling non-core assets. National copper output could recover to 5.5 million-6 million metric tons within five years from less than 5 million this year, he forecast, with new projects taking another two to three years to affect production.

CoreWeave's prospective borrowing supplied the clearest new corporate-funding development. Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group are leading a potential loan of at least $4 billion that could reach investors as soon as next week and be syndicated in phases, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. The financing is expected to use chips and related customer contracts as backing. Plans remain subject to change.

The company expects investment-grade treatment for the facility even though CoreWeave itself is junk-rated. Management's early discussions put a possible yield at 7%-7.5%. Its March $8.5 billion investment-grade facility, backed by Meta customer contracts, provides a structural comparison: one portion carries a floating margin of 2.25 percentage points over SOFR, while another was financed at a fixed rate of about 5.9%. The floating margin is only one component of its interest cost. The new loan would broaden financing access after the company's stronger sales outlook, while Chief Executive Michael Intrator continues to rule out unsecured borrowing at current rates.

Intrator also said operating income was growing faster than interest expense, forecast positive net income in 2028 and described greater use of customer prepayments as an alternative source of funding. Those are management's expectations and financing choices. D.A. Davidson's Gil Luria continued to question the business's ability to reduce debt because interest expense exceeds adjusted operating income. Separately, Bloomberg's Odd Lots account highlighted about 130,000 GPUs coming off contract in 2027 that management sees as potential additional revenue without further capital expenditure. Citi analysts led by Steph Choe argued that possible construction delays could increase the value of established facilities and development pipelines, distinguishing existing capacity from projects still awaiting completion.

Demand news from CoreWeave's customers also developed. OpenAI's Q3 revenue reached $10 billion, almost 50% above the preceding quarter and nearly three times the year-earlier level, according to people familiar with the figures. Anthropic's IPO attracted multiple times the orders for the available shares, and the Financial Times reported that bankers were considering a valuation of $1.5 trillion or more, above the initial terms. Investor Jack Selby remained skeptical, warning that an underperforming debut could catalyze a broader AI correction. Theory Ventures' Tomasz Tunguz reported more conservative revenue multiples in AI financing discussions over the past two weeks, while B Capital's Howard Morgan said he was advising startups to seek lower valuations. Stronger reported revenue and demand for one offering coexist with more selective private-capital negotiations.

Newton Commercial Finance is holding early investor discussions for a potential $180 million equipment-loan and lease securitization, with AI-chip loans making up about 15% of the collateral, according to people familiar with the plans. The Apple Bank and Eagle Point Credit Management venture expects Morningstar DBRS ratings ranging from AAA to the BB tier. The proposal follows Stonebriar's $869 million offering last month, with roughly 15% GPU exposure, and Wingspire's September transaction of more than $407 million, with about 20%. Newton's terms are not final.

Crunch Fitness is exploring about $800 million of franchise-revenue-backed financing arranged by Guggenheim Securities. The proposed structure comprises $650 million of institutionally marketed bonds with a five-year average life, a $100 million privately placed delayed-draw note and a $50 million variable funding facility. Early discussions put the five-year spread at 230-250 basis points over benchmarks, compared with 160 basis points on Planet Fitness's roughly five-year bonds in last year's securitization. Crunch's offering could begin as soon as next week, with terms still subject to change. Neighborly separately sold a $275 million offering this week, adding to activity in whole-business securitization.

Borrower-specific negotiations continued outside new issuance. A majority group of JetBlue creditors executed a cooperation agreement preventing side deals with lenders that joined the pact, according to people familiar with it. IHeartMedia is exploring the sale of some or all of its podcast business to raise cash. Blackstone is pitching a fund expected to raise at least $3 billion to buy interests in other managers' core real-estate funds at discounts to net asset value, addressing a continuing need for liquidity in that sector.

Fresh analysis of corporate-bond demand identified household income-seeking as a significant source of support. Barclays strategists led by Dominique Toublan wrote last month that individuals had put $268 billion into aggregate-index high-grade bond funds through September, almost twice the comparable 2025 amount. Corporate debt accounts for roughly a quarter of those funds' holdings. Retail investors now own about 17% of the high-grade and high-yield corporate market, the highest share since early 2022. Janus Henderson's Bradford Smith attributed part of the demand to retirees seeking long-lived income; TD Securities' Hans Mikkelsen cautioned that further price declines could undermine that appetite even when yields are attractive.

In monetary policy, Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson supplied a distinct argument for gradual tightening. Speaking Tuesday evening, the voting policymaker said wage pressures remained limited and inflation expectations consistent with the 2% target. She would favor faster action if expectations rose, wages accelerated or underlying inflation moved higher, conditions she said she was not currently observing. She described underlying inflation as stuck between 2.5% and 3% and argued that a gradual pace gives households, businesses and financial institutions time to adjust. Chicago's Austan Goolsbee, in a separate Tuesday interview, said persistent services inflation was particularly troubling and declined to constrain the choices available at the next meeting. The remarks leave pace and the conditions for acceleration as live areas of disagreement.

Britain received a more forceful independent assessment. In research published Wednesday, the National Institute of Economic and Social Research said another BOE increase would still leave inflation above 2% until the end of 2030. It called for rates to reach 5% next year to achieve control about 18 months sooner. Its concern centers on pay negotiations occurring while inflation exceeds 4% and a quarterly energy-price-cap reset that could lift household gas and electricity bills by about a quarter in January. Taylor Wimpey meanwhile forecast annual operating profit at the bottom of its £262 million-£299 million range and 10,500 completions excluding joint ventures. Its November 8 order book fell to 6,839 homes from 7,253 a year earlier as higher mortgage rates and living costs constrained buyers. Australian home lending fell a record 15.5% in Q3, adding a separate observation of weaker borrowing demand under higher rates.

U.S. mortgage applications offered a modest improvement. MBA's 30-year contract rate fell 9 basis points to 7.21% in the week ended November 6, its fourth consecutive decline. Purchase applications increased 7.5%, the strongest gain since mid-April but only the second weekly increase since late August. Refinancing rose 4.5%, its third successive gain, while remaining near the lowest level since January 2025. Total applications increased 6.2% after a 1.2% decline. The market index rose to 204.6 from 192.6, the purchase index to 141.2 from 131.4 and the refinance index to 540.7 from 517.5. These weekly observations describe housing finance before the holiday.

South Korea imposed a record 1.63 trillion won, or about $1.2 billion, cartel fine on more than a dozen banks and brokerages. The Korea Fair Trade Commission said primary dealers exchanged bid-yield information or coordinated yields and volumes in 150 government-bond auctions from January 2020 through June 2023, finding specific agreements in 145. KB Securities received the largest fine, 332.2 billion won. Criminal complaints cover seven firms: KB, NH Investment & Securities, Mirae Asset, Industrial Bank of Korea, Kiwoom, Korea Development Bank and Korea Investment & Securities. The commission said the conduct undermined competitive auctions and caused government losses, bringing a significant enforcement action to the sovereign distribution system.

Two central-bank leadership questions also advanced. Bloomberg reported internal debate over whether New York Fed President John Williams must retire in June 2027 at 65 or can remain until June 2028, completing 10 years in that role. The issue turns on the treatment of his earlier San Francisco presidency. Williams expects to serve through 2028; no formal search has been announced, and it is unclear whether Chair Kevin Warsh or the Fed board would support an earlier departure. In Canada, economists identified Jean Boivin, Jean-François Perrault, Nicolas Vincent, Carolyn Wilkins, Paul Beaudry and Carolyn Rogers as possible successors to Tiff Macklem, whose term ends in June. The bank's board appoints the governor subject to government approval; the reported candidates are early contenders.

Germany's independent economic advisers raised their 2026 growth forecast to 1.3% from May's 0.5% and their 2027 forecast to 1% from 0.8%, citing government spending and resilient exports while warning about a widening deficit. Energy supply brought another fresh observation: Saudi Arabia told OPEC that October production rose 26% to 10.56 million barrels a day, while Iraq reported almost 4.9 million barrels a day, above its agreed limits. A senior Iranian official's rejection of surrendering enriched uranium left a central obstacle to peace unresolved. Separately, Oxford Economics' El Niño vulnerability study placed Ecuador, Peru and Indonesia at the top of its exposure ranking, citing agriculture, mining and electricity-generation structures as channels through which weather shocks could affect activity and costs.

## Next Open-Session Watch

U.S. trading reopens alongside November 12 labor and housing releases. Initial claims for the week ended November 7 are expected at 195,000 after 189,000, with continuing claims for October 31 expected at 1.710 million after 1.718 million. Both arrive at 13:30 UTC. October existing-home sales follow at 15:00 UTC, with consensus at 3.85 million after 3.99 million. The closings data will show whether the recent improvement in mortgage applications is accompanied by a firmer completed-sales market.

Thursday's Fed speakers include Beth Hammack at 14:00 UTC, Michael Barr at 15:00, Goolsbee at 16:30, Mary Daly at 18:10 and Williams at 23:30. Paulson's conditions for gradual tightening and Goolsbee's concern about services prices sharpen the question of whether more officials favor accelerating the pace before the December 9 decision.

Treasury's 30-year auction is scheduled for 18:00 UTC, following the holiday interruption; four-, eight- and 17-week bills are scheduled at 16:30. The long-bond sale will provide a new observation of demand for duration. October's federal budget statement at 19:00 UTC is expected to show a $298.6 billion deficit. Fed balance-sheet and reserve-balance figures follow at 21:30 UTC.

Energy inventories at 17:00 UTC will add physical-supply evidence alongside Gulf production and unresolved diplomacy. Consensus expects a 1.1 million-barrel decline in crude stocks, a 0.1 million-barrel gasoline draw and a 1 million-barrel distillate draw for the week ended November 6. The composition matters for the persistence of fuel-cost pressure even as producers restore output.

The financing calendar extends beyond reopening. CoreWeave's potential loan will test the borrowing terms available against chips and customer contracts; Newton's equipment ABS and Crunch's franchise securitization bring different collateral and investor bases. Anthropic is due to price November 18 and begin trading November 19, putting the strength of its order book against the valuation skepticism expressed by private investors. China's planned dollar sovereign sale falls in the week of November 16. Legislative progress and the scope of any bond-interest tax in China, together with congressional treatment of Brazil's fiscal package, remain independent determinants of government funding costs.
